ACCT5906.description: Join us on a dynamic exploration of pivotal accounting concepts tailored to empower innovative business leaders. This course gives you the “Ten Most Important Things” you need to know to understand and run a successful business. We will give you the ability to be a successful manager, by applying an entrepreneurial mindset to ensure financial success. The knowledge you acquire is not only relevant, but critical for aspiring business professionals seeking to manage your own business and make informed financial decisions.
enrolment_rules_raw:
Students in programs 8409, 8415, 8413 OR in ACCTES or ACCTYS Masters of Commerce specialisations are not permitted to take this course.
Students who have taken ACCT5930 previously should not take this course.
ACCT5906.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5906.title: Financial Literacy for Business Decisions

ACCT5907.description: This course introduces analytics tools used in the analysis of financial statements to identify and understand the economic reality and strategic use of accounting numbers. You will learn to evaluate financial performance, identify sources of value creation and risk and credit assessment, and techniques used in assessing the achievement of financial targets and strategic goals. If you are aiming to become a future CFO at a leading company or a financial analyst at a top investment bank, this course is for you.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACCT5930
ACCT5907.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5907.title: International Financial Statement Analysis

ACCT5908.description: Do you want to understand the operations of a broad range of businesses and threats to the success of those businesses? Do you want to apply that knowledge to the determination of whether financial and other corporate reporting is reliable? Assurance is the cornerstone of the modern international economy as it allows investors and other stakeholders to have faith in the reliability of financial and other information produced by companies. This course will help you understand how to develop and use a comprehensive understanding of the business and its interdependencies to test the reliability of corporate reporting. You will focus on financial reporting as well as emerging and increasingly important corporate reporting on climate and other sustainability topics.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACCT5942
ACCT5908.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5908.title: Auditing and Assurance Services

ACCT5909.description: Current Developments in Auditing Research is designed to extend disciplinary perspectives in auditing and provide training for research in auditing and assurance services. The course focuses on current areas of research in auditing and related assurance services. The following topics will be covered: some of the main empirical and theoretical developments in auditing research; the main research methods used in auditing research; alternative research methods; the practical implications of current research in auditing; the relationship of research to practice and standard-setting, and statistical tools to use in audit research.
ACCT5909.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5909.title: Current Developments in Auditing Research

ACCT5910.description: This course provides you with vital skills to analyse and assess companies using data primarily obtained from corporate financial statements. Aimed at students pursuing careers in consulting, investment banking, or entrepreneurship, it enhances your capability to scrutinise financial statements and disclosures to uncover a company's core strategic traits and value drivers. You will master techniques for systematically analysing profitability and growth, and develop forecasts for earnings and cash flows. The course combines theoretical foundations with practical application through real-world case studies and exercises using financial databases. By its conclusion, you will be adept at making informed decisions regarding equity valuation, credit assessment, and debt valuation.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ((ACCT5930 or ACCT5906) AND (FINS5511 or FINS5513 or FINS5514)) OR (enrolment in program 8406)
ACCT5910.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5910.title: Business Analysis and Valuation

ACCT5919.description: This course is designed to prepare you to navigate the complexities of modern business environments, ideal for those aspiring to leadership roles or strategic management positions. In today’s global landscape, businesses face unprecedented challenges and uncertainties, including rapid technological advancements, shorter product life cycles, heightened customer and societal expectations, and various internal and external risks. This course provides a comprehensive exploration of business risk management, addressing key risks that impact value creation such as competition, financial constraints, regulatory and legal requirements, corporate leadership issues, strategy execution, and organisational capabilities. Through a blend of conceptual frameworks, technical skills, and speculative approaches, students will gain a deep understanding of how to identify, assess, and manage these risks. Case studies and research are integral to the curriculum, offering practical insights and real-world applications. By the end of this course, you will be well-equipped to contribute to an organisations' resilience and sustainability in an ever-changing global environment.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite or Corequisite: ACCT5930 or COMM5003 or ACCT5906
ACCT5919.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5919.title: Business Risk Management

ACCT5920.description: In today’s dynamic business landscape, intangible assets account for ninety percent of market capitalisation. This course provides hands-on experience and tools and frameworks to measure and evaluate these assets, including the Balanced Scorecard. You will learn to translate complex data into meaningful narratives through real-world cases and explore concepts like Reputation Quotients and Net Promoter Scores. Understanding the constitution and value of intangible assets is crucial for business success because it allows companies to better leverage their intellectual property, reputation, and customer relationships, leading to more informed decision-making and sustained competitive advantage.
ACCT5920.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5920.title: Managing Intangible Resources

ACCT5925.description: This course focuses on the drivers of Enterprise Value creation, emphasizing the need for changes in business decision-making and reporting. It explores the significance of intangible value drivers, including ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) factors, and the growing importance of the Integrated Reporting Framework for responsible decision-making and transparent reporting on enterprise value over the short, medium and long-term. With ESG reporting gaining traction among investors and new sustainability accounting and reporting standards, the course demonstrates how Integrated Reporting enhances communication of performance and future prospects, enabling more sustainable value creation. Highly interactive with practical illustrations and case studies, this course prepares participants for careers in leading accounting, sustainability and consulting firms, Government and regulatory bodies, NGOs, and innovative corporations, all demanding expertise in sustainable business practices and corporate responsibility.
ACCT5925.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5925.title: ESG Reporting and Enterprise Value Creation

ACCT5930.description: Accounting is the language of business, and this course is designed for future professionals in the accounting and finance field and entrepreneurs needing a solid foundation in financial accounting principles. This course will provide you with the foundations to prepare financial statements and communicate the financial impact of business events or decisions. You will also learn to interpret the key financial statements as well as sustainability performance to facilitate informed decision-making.
enrolment_rules_raw: Students who have previously completed ACCT5906 should not enrol into this course.
ACCT5930.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5930.title: Financial Accounting

ACCT5931.description: In the words of Chanticleer at the Australian Financial Review (2024): “Making money is hard, let alone doing it when the goalposts are shifting around”. In the ESG (environmental, social and governance) era, sustainability matters – and it shift the goalposts for organisations. Whether you’re studying to become a sustainability consultant, financial analyst, business leader or young investor, this course will enable you to develop, analyse and evaluate business strategies to create sustainable value. We’ll bring strategy together with the numbers to look at financial, environmental, social and governance performance. Completing the course, you’ll be equipped to make business decisions using a sustainable performance lens, and considering different stakeholder perspectives.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (Completion of ACCT5996 and enrolled in 8409 or 8415 or 8413) OR (Completion of 42 UOC and ACCT5996 and enrolled in 8404 or 8417 or 8544 or 8339)
ACCT5931.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5931.title: Sustainable Management Accounting

ACCT5935.description:
Ethics and governance are core components of the knowledge and skill base of professional accounting.  As key business decision-makers, accountants must be proficient in regulatory regimes, compliance requirements and government mechanisms to ensure lawful, ethical and effective corporate behaviour and operations.  Furthermore, today's professional accountants are involved with leadership and management more than ever, and are directly involved in many important decisions.  An understanding of ethics and governance is thus essential.

This course provides students with the analytical and decision-making skills and knowledge to identify and resolve professional and ethical issues they may face in future.

This course is delivered in conjunction with CPA Australia.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415), OR (Enrolment in 5415)
ACCT5935.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5935.title: CPA Ethics and Governance

ACCT5936.description:
This course is designed to provide you with financial reporting and business skills that are applicable in an international professional environment, based on the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRSs). 

In a competitive international environment, financial reporting provides users with information to formulate corporate strategies, business plans and leadership initiatives. Members of the accounting profession who provide assurance services also require a good understanding of the financial reporting, IFRSs. Directors are also required to state that the financial statements are fairly stated. These examples reinforce the importance of financial reporting. 

This course is delivered in conjunction with CPA Australia.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of (ACCT5930, ACCT5931, ACCT5942, ACCT5943, ACCT5996, ECON5258, FINS5511 and TABL5543) OR (Enrolment in 5415).
ACCT5936.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5936.title: CPA Financial Reporting

ACCT5937.description:
Strategic management accounting is a key component of the overall skills base of today’s professional accountant. This course examines the management accountant’s strategic and value creating role in dynamic organisations operating in the global business environment.

This course highlights the management accounting tools and techniques of value chain analysis and project management that have become increasingly important in contemporary operating environments.

This course is delivered in conjunction with CPA Australia.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of (ACCT5930, ACCT5931, ACCT5942, ACCT5943, ACCT5996, ECON5258, FINS5511 and TABL5543) OR (Enrolment in 5415).
ACCT5937.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5937.title: CPA Strategic Management Accounting

ACCT5938.description:
This course consolidates and builds on the learnings candidates have gained in the other three prerequisite courses: Ethics and Governance, Financial Reporting and Strategic Management Accounting.

In the increasingly complex business environment in which organisations operate, characterised by change, uncertainty and escalating competition, the disciplines of strategy and leadership have become critical to successful organisational performance. This course links the knowledge expected of the future finance professional to the concepts of strategy and leadership.

The course materials address the needs of accounting professionals operating in different international markets in varying roles, and in relation to current and emerging technologies and emerging business models.

This course is delivered in conjunction with CPA Australia.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPAA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415) OR (Enrolment in 5415). Students must also have completed ACCT5935, ACCT5936, and ACCT5937.
ACCT5938.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5938.title: CPA Global Strategy and Leadership

ACCT5942.description: ACCT5942 is an advanced course designed to decode the complexities of financial reporting within large, complex corporations, particularly those with subsidiaries, significant investments in other companies and joint venture projects with other entities. It aims to provide you with the necessary skills to prepare and analyse detailed financial reports, simulating the role of a Chief Financial Officer or financial analyst within a multinational corporation. This course delves into accounting for business combinations, consolidated financial reports, equity accounting, accounting for joint ventures, translation of foreign currency financial statements and the intricacies of accounting for company income tax, making it an essential toolkit for anyone aspiring to excel in the financial domain of complex business structures.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACCT5930
ACCT5942.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5942.title: Corporate Accounting and Regulation

ACCT5943.description: The primary objectives of the course are to provide students with applied knowledge in financial reporting. Through relevant theoretical lenses, the course aims to enhance students' practical skills in applying the Australian equivalents of international financial reporting standards that cover specific industries, contexts, and financial statement items. Students will gain an appreciation of the conceptual strengths and weaknesses of required accounting methods and the motivations underlying the choices made by directors and managers in circumstances where flexibilities are permitted in the accounting standards. The course will build students' capacity in critically evaluating controversial issues in external reporting and in contributing to debates on the usefulness and value relevance of financial reporting.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACCT5930 and Corequisite: ACCT5942
ACCT5943.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5943.title: Advanced Financial Reporting

ACCT5946.description: High levels of debt exist across the world following the Global Financial Crisis. Combined with slow economic growth this has created a volatile global economic environment. As a result, organisations are vulnerable to financial risk, including funding and liquidity risk, market risk from interest rate, exchange rate or commodity price movements, credit risk and operational risk. The purpose of this course is to equip you with the necessary skills to assess these financial risks and manage them strategically with the use of financial instruments.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415), OR (Enrolment in 5415)
ACCT5946.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5946.title: CPA Financial Risk Management

ACCT5947.description:
In today’s rapidly evolving digital landscape, including a vast array of new capabilities and use cases, accounting and finance professionals must stay ahead of both the opportunities and challenges presented by emerging technologies and the ways in which they are utilised to disrupt extant industry practices.

It is imperative to learn to recognise and reap the full benefit of these technologies and the digital finance environment. This course explores the knowledge and skills necessary to understand and navigate the complex world of digital finance and provides the tools to apply emerging technologies in a real-world context.

More specifically, the course discusses the topics of: the digital finance ecosystem; the future of money; technology and its use in finance; data analytics, interpretation and visualization; and risk management, governance and regulation.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415), OR (Enrolment in 5415). Students must also have completed ACCT5935, ACCT5936, ACCT5937, and (ACCT5908 OR ACCT3708 OR equivalent course credit).
ACCT5947.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5947.title: CPA Digital Finance

ACCT5948.description:
This course is designed to provide you with an awareness of the key provisions of the relevant taxation legislation and enable you to apply the relevant legislative concepts to determine taxation consequences. It also introduces fundamental concepts of income tax law and provides an in-depth understanding of relevant Australian tax laws and their application in the areas of income tax law for individuals and simple business structures, capital gains tax, goods and services tax, and fringe benefits tax.

This course also covers the tax administration system, and the ethical and professional obligations a tax adviser.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of (ACCT5930, ACCT5931, ACCT5942, ACCT5943, ACCT5996, ECON5258, FINS5511 and TABL5543) OR (Enrolment in 5415).
ACCT5948.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5948.title: CPA Australia Taxation

ACCT5949.description: This course is tailored for aspiring managers and professionals eager to refine their resource management skills in today’s fast-paced and competitive business landscape. Through a curated mix of contemporary and foundational readings, you will learn to effectively mobilize resources to foster and maintain organizational agility. By the end of the course, you’ll gain a deeper understanding of how agile organizations operate, enabling you to critically reflect on and shape relevant practices. This knowledge prepares you for future leadership roles, by enabling you to be a more effective manager in driving and leading agile organizations.
ACCT5949.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5949.title: Managing Agile Organisations

ACCT5951.description: Review of alternative approaches to the development of theories in external reporting. Explication and evaluation of substantive theories and associated research studies. Examination of research findings related to the accounting and reporting environment, agency cost and financial contracting, the properties of reported accounting numbers, predictive value of accounting information, the use of information in capital markets, and the use of accounting reports by individual decision makers.

equivalents.title: Current Developments in Accounting Research - Financial

ACCT5951.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5951.title: Current Developments in Accounting Research - Financial

ACCT5952.description: The aim of this course is to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of contemporary management accounting research, which emanates from different philosophical perspectives and employs different theories and research methods. Research is divided into two broad streams: work that seeks (a) to explain and design, and (b) to understand and interpret the practice of management accounting in organisation and societies.

equivalents.title: Current Developments in Accounting Research - Managerial

ACCT5952.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5952.title: Current Developments in Accounting Research - Managerial

ACCT5955.description: Learn how to design, implement, and utilise management control systems for better management and decision-making around organizational resources and operations. This course provides a strategic and executive perspective on how MCS work and are changing with new business models, new technologies, digitalisation and increasingly blurred organizational boundaries. You’ll engage with industry examples and apply proven frameworks to solve real-world business challenges. Through this course, you’ll develop critical thinking and leadership skills in leveraging MCS to effectively navigate modern organisational complexities and drive business success.
ACCT5955.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5955.title: Management Control Systems in Contemporary Contexts

ACCT5961.description:
Climate change and sustainability are key challenges for our society and economy today and these areas provide great opportunities for future employment. Governments and non-governmental organisations around the world have engaged in various climate change and adaptation policy initiatives to ensure survival and prosperity of current and future generations.

This course explores issues related to reporting on climate change and sustainability and its implications for businesses. As the course is offered in the Business faculty, it is only appropriate to focus on business activities with ethical and social significance that are often omitted from conventional profit-oriented business transactions. Insights on established and proposed policy frameworks will provide students with an overview of sustainability reporting and the ability to start preparing a sustainability report in their current or future employment. Impact of the recent establishment of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) by the IFRS Foundation will be covered particularly the release of sustainability standards and how Australia is responding to this generational shift in business reporting. This course will be useful for students who aspire to work in leading accounting and consulting firms and climate and sustainability advisors.
ACCT5961.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5961.title: Reporting for Climate Change and Sustainability

ACCT5967.description: To assist MCom Hons students in completion of research project requirement. May consist of an examinable readings program defined to meet the needs of a particular student or a formal program undertaken by a group of students whose research projects are in a common area.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACCT5997 or equivalent
ACCT5967.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5967.title: Special Topic in Accounting

ACCT5972.description: Analytics combined with accounting data is at the heart of most forward-looking corporate decisions. Investment bankers, equity research analysts, portfolio managers, credit analysts, lenders, and capital market regulators rely on accounting data to identify investment opportunities, assess business risks, and negotiate business contracts. This course will help you gain basic understanding of how professionals use analytics tools to leverage accounting data to produce significant insights and make meaningful predictions. Most importantly, you will learn how accounting analytics are applied in real-world business contexts, such as quantitative investing, financial fraud prediction, earnings forecasting, etc. You will use numerous real-word case studies in lectures, tutorials, and assessments to reinforce your learnings.
ACCT5972.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5972.title: Accounting Analytics for Business Decision Making

ACCT5995.description: Do you want to investigate fraud, protect and safeguard businesses from fraud? This course will arm you with the expertise to safeguard businesses against the pervasive threat of fraud. You will learn to detect and prevent fraud, learn why fraud occurs and learn the latest fraud investigation methods and techniques.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACCT5906 or ACCT5930
ACCT5995.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5995.title: Fraud Examination Fundamentals

ACCT5996.description: Take a deep dive into business activities to learn how to make informed and effective decisions with the resources at your disposal. In this course, you will explore the creation and use of management accounting information to analyse business activities and drive operational improvement. You will develop skills to enhance your business acumen in managing costs and resources and identify sources of value creation for superior, sustainable performance. Adopting an active learning approach, this course utilizes student-led discussions, individual and team-based activities, and real-world applications to empower you to engage more effectively with organizational planning, control and process improvement for more efficient and effective business operations.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite or Corequisite: ACCT5930 or COMM5003 or ACCT5906
ACCT5996.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5996.title: Management Accounting and Business Analysis

ACCT5997.description: This course considers the relationship between science and scientific method; reviews some of the research methods commonly used to conduct research in accounting; and provides an introduction to the interpretation of the key statistical techniques used in accounting research.
ACCT5997.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5997.title: Seminar in Research Methodology

ACCT5998.description: Please contact the school for further information.
ACCT5998.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5998.title: Project Seminar

ACCT5999.description: Please contact the school for further information.
ACCT5999.school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
ACCT5999.title: Project Report

ACTL5004.description: Students complete a project under the direction of a supervisor.
ACTL5004.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5004.title: Project Report - Actuarial Studies

ACTL5100.description: This course, along with ACTL5200, aligns with the Actuarial Control Cycle in the Actuary Program of the Actuaries Institute. It develops the theory and practice behind the actuarial management of risk-based and other products offered by financial institutions. Using examples from actuarial practice, the course covers implications for life insurance, general insurance, superannuation, asset-liability management, and other areas where actuaries are involved in product design, pricing, reserving, investment, and surplus management. The course emphasizes recent advancements in actuarial theory and practice.
enrolment_rules_raw:
Pre-requisites: ECON5103 and ACTL5108 and ACTL5109 and ACTL5106 and 60+ WAM
Co-requisites: ACTL5104 and ACTL5105
ACTL5100.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5100.title: Actuarial Theory and Practice  A

ACTL5101.description: This course examines the probability and statistics essential for actuarial studies. It explores a range of topics, including univariate and multivariate random variables, moments, probability generating functions, and moment generating functions. Additionally, the curriculum addresses marginal and conditional distributions, sampling distributions, estimation techniques and hypothesis testing. Practical examples from actuarial studies, finance, and insurance are incorporated to demonstrate the real-world applications of the concepts discussed.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in program 8411 or 8416 or 7480

equivalents.title: Waiver for ACTL5101 Probability and Statistics for Actuaries

ACTL5101.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5101.title: Probability and Statistics for Actuaries

ACTL5102.description: This course covers the financial mathematics necessary for analyzing financial and insurance transactions. Key topics include the mathematics of compound interest, the analysis and valuation of annuities, bonds, loans, and derivative securities; yield curves and immunization strategies; and an introduction to stochastic interest rate models and their actuarial applications.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in program 8411 or 8416 or 7480.
ACTL5102.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5102.title: Financial Mathematics

ACTL5103.description: This course discusses actuarial models for stochastic modelling of liabilities and assets, demonstrating their use in actuarial practice. The course will cover topics such as Markov chains in both discrete-time and continuous-time settings, focusing on their application to experience rating; Markov process models and their applications in areas such as insurance, financial risk, survival, sickness, and marriage models; Monte Carlo methods for simulating stochastic processes; and the estimation of Markov chains. Students are expected to implement these models using R software in a numerical computing environment.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACTL5101 and (enrolment in program 8411 or 8416 or 7480)
ACTL5103.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5103.title: Stochastic Modelling for Actuaries

ACTL5104.description: This course covers the actuarial profession syllabus for survival models, focusing on understanding and predicting mortality, morbidity, and longevity risks. It applies these techniques to life, health, and disability insurance, superannuation, finance, and epidemiology. These models help forecast risks related to events such as mortality, health changes, and credit defaults, leading to better risk quantification, pricing, and management. Key topics include: survival models and actuarial notation; Estimation of lifetime distributions; Maximum likelihood estimation of transition intensities in multi-state models, considering age and duration; graduation of crude estimates and tests for fidelity and smoothness; and models for projecting mortality trends. The course emphasizes implementing these concepts using numerical computer packages. Additionally, it will address ethical considerations and issues related to discrimination and heterogeneity in mortality and health risks.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACTL5101 and (enrolment in program 8411 or 8416 or 7480)

equivalents.title: Modelling and Prediction of Life and Health Related Risks

ACTL5104.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5104.title: Survival Analysis and Prediction of Life and Health Related Risks

ACTL5105.description: This course covers the actuarial mathematics, models and techniques for valuing long-term contingent cashflows. In-depth understanding of valuation of claims is a key aspect of actuarial work, specifically in the areas of life insurance, health, disability insurance, superannuation and pensions, as well as broader financial institutions. This course combines the present value principle with various stochastic tools in pricing, reserving, cashflow projection and profit testing tasks for various products in life insurance, health and disability, and pension and superannuation space. The fundamental techniques covered in the course help insurers to adequately price and manage the risks of various contracts in life insurance and pension systems, hence allowing the creation of products to help individuals manage risks. They are also increasingly applied in broader areas including social protection and government policy.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACTL5101 and ACTL5102 and (enrolment in program 8411 or 8416 or 7480)

exclusions.title: Actuarial Mathematics for Insurance and Superannuation

ACTL5105.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5105.title: Life Insurance and Superannuation

ACTL5106.description: This course focuses on the principles and mathematical models that describe the random quantities and processes in general insurance practice. It invovles constructing mathematical models and utilising historical data to predict futgure insurance costs and risks. Key areas of study include data analysis, loss models, reinsurance treaties, premium calculation, claims reserving, ruin theory, Bayesian inference, and credibility theory.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACTL5101 and ACTL5103 and (enrolment in program 8411 or 8416 or 7480)
ACTL5106.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5106.title: Insurance Risk Models

ACTL5108.description: The aim of the course is to provide the future actuary with a basic understanding of corporate finance and financial reporting. The course will cover the instruments used by companies to raise finance and manage financial risk and will develop an understanding of how to interpret the accounts and financial statements of companies and financial institutions.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolled in 8411 or 8416 or 7480.

equivalents.title: Waiver for ACTL5108 Finance and Financial Reporting for Actuaries

ACTL5108.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5108.title: Finance and Financial Reporting for Actuaries

ACTL5109.description: The aim of this course is to introduce the mathematical and economic models of financial economics used by actuaries and to overview their application to asset-liability management. The topics are illustrated with applications to the valuation, actuarial and risk management of insurance and superannuation contracts especially those with embedded options and financial guarantees.
enrolment_rules_raw:
Prerequisite: ACTL5101 and ACTL5102 and (enrolment in 8411 or 8416 or 7480)
Corequisite: ACTL5103
ACTL5109.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5109.title: Financial Economics for Insurance and Superannuation

ACTL5110.description: This course covers the actuarial professional syllabus for data analysis and statistics for risk modelling, focusing on techniques for analysing mortality, health, and insurance data used in actuarial decision-making. The course includes exploratory data analysis, data checking and cleaning, and data visualization. Students will learn classification and prediction techniques using regression and generalized linear models, as well as descriptive, inferential, and predictive analysis models. The course will also delve into statistical and machine learning, covering both supervised and unsupervised learning methods. The course also addresses ethical, regulatory, and professional issues, along with risks and risk management associated with data analysis. Special emphasis is placed on effectively communicating technical results for business applications.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACTL5101

exclusions.title: Statistical Machine Learning for Risk and Actuarial Applications

ACTL5110.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5110.title: Statistical Machine Learning for Risk and Actuarial Applications

ACTL5111.description: This course will introduce students to Artificial Intelligence techniques, with particular focus on deep learning and applications to risk and insurance. Particular importance will be on various deep learning algorithms and how they can be combined with other actuarial techniques in order to solve business problems in insurance and risk management including in pricing, reserving, capital management, and insurance business processes improvements. Ethical considerations of AI models will also be discussed. Students will be expected to understand the deep learning algorithms considered, their relationship with other actuarial techniques, as well as be able to fit and evaluate various deep learning models for actuarial applications using appropriate software.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACTL5101
ACTL5111.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5111.title: Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning Models for Risk and Insurance

ACTL5200.description: This course, along with ACTL5100, aligns with the Actuarial Control Cycle in the Actuary Program of the Actuaries Institute. It explores the theory and practice fundamental to the actuarial management of risk-based and other financial institution products. The course utilizes examples from actuarial practice and addresses implications for life insurance, general insurance, superannuation, asset-liability management, and other areas where actuaries engage in product design, pricing, reserving, investment, and surplus management. Emphasis is placed on recent developments in actuarial theory and practice.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ACTL5100 and 60+ WAM
ACTL5200.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5200.title: Actuarial Theory and Practice B

ACTL5301.description: Recent occurrences of significant losses in the financial and insurance markets associated with catastrophic events such as heatwaves, floods, cyclones, bushfires, and earthquakes have intensified the need for a systematic approach to modelling, measuring, and managing catastrophe risks. Culprits behind catastrophe risks include frequency, severity, and dependence. This course introduces students to advanced statistical and actuarial models for a variety of risks in financial institutions such as banks, insurance/reinsurance companies, and superannuation funds. Traditional and newly emerging risks encountered therein will be studied, with a special focus on extreme losses, extreme dependence, and loss aggregation over time. Topics covered include: risk measures; multivariate models; copulas and dependence; financial time series; extreme value theory; market credit and operational risk. Students will be implementing the models using computer software.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisites: ACTL5103 or program 4520
ACTL5301.school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
ACTL5301.title: Quantitative Risk Management Techniques

ACTL5305.description: This course covers the actuarial professional associateship syllabus for the actuarial data science principles. It combines data analytics and modelling concepts with the practical applications of modern analytical tools and techniques, as well as their actuarial applications. This course covers the key iterative steps involved in building a model - business understanding, data understanding and preparation, modelling, evaluation, communication and deployment. Particular focus will be on the selection of appropriate predictive modelling techniques for a stated situation and how to evaluate the suitability of a model, taking into account business context and objectives, as well as on the communication of modelling results to a range of business decision making audiences.

ACTL5305.title: Actuarial Data Science Applications

ACTL6106.description: This course equips research-focused and PhD-level students in risk and actuarial studies with rigorous quantitative and conceptual tools to critically design, assess, and govern ethical AI systems in complex, high-stakes environments, such as insurance and financial services. Students will investigate the deeper methodological and societal challenges involved in embedding fairness, accountability, transparency, and robustness into the AI development process. Through a combination of theoretical frameworks, frontier research, quantitative tools, and real-world case studies, the course fosters critical reflection on ethical principles, regulatory implications, and professional responsibilities. It prepares students to lead the development of ethically sound AI solutions and contribute to scholarly and policy debates in responsible AI.

AERO9500.description: This course gives an overview of satellite systems, describing their main applications and providing a detailed introduction into the principles of orbital mechanics. The course focuses on orbital mechanics, covering orbit description and analysis, perturbations, orbital manoeuvres, interplanetary transfers and launch systems.
enrolment_rules_raw: Exclusion: AERO4500
AERO9500.school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
AERO9500.title: Space Systems Architectures and Orbits

AERO9610.description: This course gives the students a basis in the design issues involved in the engineering of the space segment in order to enable to fulfil the mission.  This course covers three areas of the space segment design: 1. Design methodology for satellites; 2. Operational environment, including thermal, structural, electromagnetic environment; 3. Hardware/devices/components introduction of the space segment, incorporating the payload types and satellite supporting subsystems. Examples of current and past space missions are used to illustrate the design process and design implementation associated with the space segment of the mission. Where appropriate, theory associated with the preliminary analysis of the operation and performance of the space segment is also presented. This course delivers to the student a broad overview of the engineering principles involved with the design, development, testing and implementation of the space segment of a space mission.
AERO9610.school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
AERO9610.title: The Space Segment

AERO9660.description:
This is a continuation of AERO3660 Flight Performance and Propulsion looking at advanced aspects of propulsion. It further builds on MMAN2700 Thermodynamics.

We start by conduction, convection, and radiation modes of heat transfer as our more advanced propulsion systems will require cooling. In detail, we look into a more detailed heat exchanger analysis than what was done in MMAN2700 Thermodynamics and we consider the Meredith effect.

We take the basic analysis of the turbojet engine and extend it to analyse the two-spool turbofan gas turbine engine. We also analyse propelling nozzles suitable for commercial and military aircraft. We also have a detailed look at Ramjets and Scramjets.

The work on rocketry is new. You will be introduced to rocket engines and rocket nozzle performance. To aid in our understanding we consider high temperature gas analysis, van der Waals equation of state and other more advanced equations of state.We pay a lot of attention to liquid rocket combustion, the prediction of adiabatic flame temperature of high-temperature reacting systems, the effects of chemical equilibrium on the adiabatic flame temperature. We also consider the burning regimes of solid rocket boosters.

To complete the work on rocketry, we consider electrothermal thrusters, , nuclear rockets, ion thrusters and their optimization.

Today, electrification and partial electrification of aircraft is gaining in importance. We consider hybrid powertrains, batteries, proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell system analysis, electric machines (motors), boost converters for aircraft. We also take into account energy harvesting, the Betz limit, the Peukert effect, Paschen's law.

To finish up, we consider exergy analysis, internal combustion engines, and turbulent jet ignition.
AERO9660.school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
AERO9660.title: Advanced Aerospace Propulsion

AGSM6131.description:
This course provides an introduction to the topic of leadership. It aims to help students to build the confidence, knowledge and skills to engage in effective leadership in a broad range of contexts. It also provides guidance on self-leadership and actively managing the process of growing as a leader.

The course defines ‘leadership’ not as a position but as a process of influence that delivers direction, alignment of activities towards that direction, and personal commitment to collective success. As such, leadership is potentially relevant to all students who wish to exert influence and foster change.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs - 7316 Management, 7416 Leadership, 7417 Strategic Management, 8356 Business Administration (Executive), 8625 Business Administration (Part-time), 9225 Law/Business Administration (Part-time)
AGSM6131.title: Leadership

AGSM6143.description:
NOTE:This course was previously identified as MBAX9143.

This course aims to equip you with the skills, knowledge and experience to formulate, evaluate and implement value-creating strategies for organisations. The course introduces you to the contemporary principles, tools and frameworks of strategic management that support the work of successful strategists in leading sustainable organisations. Whether you work in small or large organisations, whether in a startup, scale up or incumbent, domestically focused or a major international or global organisation, in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors, strategic management plays a central role in achieving the objectives of the organisation as we navigate an increasingly complex, disrupted, technology-infused, and dynamic business environment.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in one of the following programs: Management (7316); Strategic Management (7417); Business Administration (Executive) (8355 or 8356); MBAX (8625); LLM/MBA(Law) (9225)
AGSM6143.title: Strategy

AGSM6210.description:
NOTE:This course was previously identified as MNGT6210.

The aim of this course is to show how the effective use of financial information can improve organisational decision-making. The course provides a broad introduction to how accounting contributes to an organisation. You will examine how accounting can help managers measure and analyse their organisation's economic performance, to improve resource allocation, and build accountability for performance through effective governance.

The users of accounting information are typically classified as either external (such as investors or lenders) or internal (such as operational managers). Different users have different  information needs. This course deals with the needs of these two main user groups and how senior managers can more effectively use accounting data to connect with them.

The course explores accounting techniques and terminology, to equip you with sufficient conceptual and practical skills to make you confident in your ability to understand and communicate complex financial strategies.

You will also examine the design and operation of accounting systems. As a result, the course integrates ideas and concepts from accounting with a range of other disciplines and reveals how the effective use of financial information provided by such systems can improve organisational decision-making. You will also examine how firms use non-financial information such as Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) to communicate their performance and strategies.

It is assumed that participants have little prior knowledge of accounting and financial management.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in one of the following programs: Management (7316); MBAE (8355 or 8356); MBAX (8625); LLM/MBAX (9225)
AGSM6210.title: Accounting and Financial Management

AGSM6234.description:
This course is designed to provide a broad strategic perspective on issues and challenges related to incorporating data analytics and AI into business decision-making for strategic gain and meaningful change.

Due to the complex and multi-faceted nature of the world of analytics, leaders and managers need some basic and abstract familiarity with the technical building blocks of analytics. This enables them to speak the language of analytics with fluency. Also, since emerging tools and objects in the world of AI and analytics are underpinned by these technical building blocks, this familiarity enables leaders and managers to separate hype from reality with confidence and make better decisions when integrating analytics/AI into their organisations.

We deliver this course in three phases to provide an integrated strategic–technical–execution view of data analytics. In Phase 1, we will explore the concept of data strategy and its connection to business strategy. In Phase 2, we aim to help you understand basic analytics and statistical concepts, building technical confidence to distinguish between hype and reality in analytics and AI, while learning to speak the language of analytics fluently. In Phase 3, we will address the challenges of incorporating analytics and AI into organisations and explore their potential to create business value and drive innovative changes in business processes.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in one of the following programs: Management (7316), Digital Innovation (7415), Technology Management (7418); MBAE (8355 or 8356); MBAX (8625); LLM/MBA(Law) (9225)

equivalents.title: Data Analysis and Statistical Modelling for Business

AGSM6234.title: Data Analytics and Decision-making

AGSM6251.description:
NOTE:This course was previously identified as MNGT6251.

At the core of every successful business model are the organisation’s value propositions. Leaders of contemporary organisations must understand how the organisation creates and manages value propositions based on understanding the wants and needs of key stakeholders. This list of stakeholders includes existing and potential customers (a.k.a. clients or funding bodies), employees, suppliers, partners or collaborators, investors, government/regulators, and communities. Doing this successfully means that through appreciating the impacts of complex conditions in the external environment, contemporary leaders are better able to create, communicate, deliver, and sustain value for their stakeholders, and capture value for the organisation. This requires an understanding of the core processes and practices of marketing management.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in one of the following programs: Management (7316); MBAE (8355 or 8356); MBAX (8625); LLM/MBAX (9225).
AGSM6251.title: Marketing Management

AGSM6275.description:
The organisations we work in are rich and complex entities in which many interactions, relationships and processes are played out every day. The complexity of these elements often poses challenges in understanding and management.

Managing People and Organisations (MPO) is focused on managers who manage people – some you manage formally, such as your subordinates, and others informally, such as your peers and bosses. Central to the course is the characterisation and discussion of everyday functions and roles in which managers take part. These include sense-making, decision-making, leading, motivating, planning, organising, mentoring, monitoring and influencing. We also address the context in which managers function and examine the effect of current issues they face. These include an increased emphasis on entrepreneurship; managing with social responsibility and the role of ethics; leading diverse, equitable and inclusive teams, and managing in a global environment. Each Unit in this course covers a topic that contributes to your undertaking these managerial roles more effectively so that you can become a better manager of yourself, others, teams and organisations.

In this course, we will ask you to test your understanding of the concepts that we introduce by examining your working life. This could involve analysing your actions, the actions of others, processes that occur within your organisation and key organisational elements. You can use these activities to evaluate the concepts by asking yourself:

  • how useful is this idea to me?
  • how can I modify this idea in light of my own experiences?
  • how can I apply this idea to my own organisation?

MPO will introduce you to some of the key concepts, issues and debates in management, offering a glimpse into various topics that could individually constitute full courses. It is intended to serve as a foundation for your understanding of management and managing others, marking the beginning of your learning journey rather than its conclusion.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in one of the following programs:- Management (7316); Leadership (7416); MBAE (8355 or 8356); MBAX (8625); LLM/MBAX (9225)
AGSM6275.title: Managing People and Organisations
