CVEN9822.description: A course on the advanced analysis and design of structural elements for students looking towards a career in Structural Engineering. The main topics of this course are the design and analysis of steel connections and composite structures that are made from steel and concrete. The course will build on your knowledge in structural steel design to introduce you to detailed design of bolt and weld connections and the design of pin connections. It will also combine and utilise the knowledge gained in previous courses of structural design to allow the design and analysis of composite steel-concrete structures including beams, slabs and columns at the serviceability and strength limit states.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Completion of 48 UOC
CVEN9822.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9822.title: Steel and Composite Structures

CVEN9824.description: In Advanced Materials Technology, details of concrete components including cement, aggregate, and admixtures will be covered. Hydration reactions in cement and structures of cement pastes will be discussed and then the properties of fresh and hardened concrete will be introduced. In addition, this course includes details of mix design of concrete. Durability issues and chemical deterioration of concrete materials (corrosion, alkali silica reaction, and sulphate attack) will be introduced and their mitigation methods will be discussed. This course also includes several topics for the sustainability: new sustainable alternative binders, low carbon concrete and high-performance concrete materials.
CVEN9824.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9824.title: Advanced Materials Technology

CVEN9826.description:
A course in advanced mechanics of structures and materials students that require, or desire, a higher capability in the application of elasticity, plasticity and fracture analysis of structures and structural materials. This subject is targeted to students desiring a greater understanding of structural mechanics and materials. The course includes lectures in the following: elasticity; plasticity; and fracture of brittle materials such as cementitious materials, fibre reinforced concrete and bond.

Higher Degree Research students should contact their school's HDR Officer to organise enrolment into this course.
CVEN9826.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9826.title: Advanced Mechanics of Structures and Materials

CVEN9840.description:
Structural health monitoring (SHM) refers to the process of design and implementing a condition monitoring and characterization strategy for engineering structures. Needs for optimization of maintenance costs, objective and science-based inspection practices, increase of safety, emergence of new and improved construction materials and methods, new developments in measurement, sensing, processing and monitoring, as well as recent technological developments in various branches of science and engineering led to creation of relatively new, interdisciplinary branch of engineering – Structural Health Monitoring. SHM examines the use of low-cost, long term monitoring systems to keep civil infrastructure under constant surveillance, ensuring structural integrity. It has received great deal of attention all over the world due to its significant impact on safety and longevity of the structures. 

This subject provides an introduction and motivation of SHM with a systematic approach to SHM process. It introduces the topics with basic definitions of measurement and monitoring, various available and emerging monitoring technologies, data acquisition systems and instrumentation, passive and active sensing technologies. The course will cover the principal methods used for local non-destructive evaluation (NDE) and global vibration based SHM techniques. Overview of signal processing basics, feature extraction and a comprehensive list of comparative features will be addressed. Brief overview of structural dynamics will be presented. The students will be provided with hands-on experience in experimental and operational modal analysis, and will learn with structural properties extraction from data. Basics on data interpretation and analysis for both static and dynamic monitoring are presented. It will also introduce students to the concepts of statistical pattern recognition, machine learning, artificial intelligence and neural network and demonstrate the application of these technologies to SHM. Techniques based on data-driven approach and model-based approach to develop SHM solutions are presented. Techniques of combining finite element modelling and field measurements for realistic loading simulations and spatial extrapolation of measured data are discussed and finally, real-world applications and current state of the technology are discussed.
CVEN9840.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9840.title: Structural Health Monitoring Fundamentals and Practices

CVEN9855.description: The effects of impurities in water and wastewater on its suitability for various beneficial uses, and methods used for detecting impurities. Analytical methods used in water and wastewater treatment for monitoring and process.

equivalents.title: Water and Wastewater Analysis and  Quality Requirements

CVEN9855.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9855.title: Water and Wastewater Analysis and Quality Requirements

CVEN9856.description: Integrated design of facilities for the treatment of various types of raw water to meet specified water quality, with emphasis on water for municipal supply, including: chemical selection, dosing and mixing; coagulation - flocculation - clarification - filtration and disinfection technology. Processes for water softening, iron and manganese removal and demineralisation, including precipitation, oxidation, ion exchange and reverse osmosis. Taste and odour control. Disposal of water treatment residuals.
CVEN9856.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9856.title: Water Treatment

CVEN9857.description: Wastewater treatment is crucial to sustaining the human population. Releasing untreated wastewater into the environment has detrimental impacts on human and environmental health from exposure to human pathogens to eutrophication of waterways. Wastewater also contains materials that can be considered resources. Wastewater engineers play roles in designing industrial and municipal wastewater treatment systems (upgrades or from scratch) to meet license standards. They also help solve operating issues and strive to minimise costs and environmental impacts. In this course we take a deep dive into wastewater engineering including process modelling to ensure graduates have a solid understanding of the principals behind unit operations and processes so that you can contribute to the upgrade and design of the treatment plants on which our civilisation is dependent.
CVEN9857.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9857.title: Wastewater Treatment

CVEN9872.description: Characterisation of municipal solid waste; collection; transfer stations; waste minimisation and recycling; waste treatment, including size reduction, composing, incineration, emerging technologies; landfill disposal, including preparation of landfill management plans and operational aspects; introduction to planning of waste management systems.
CVEN9872.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9872.title: Solid Waste Management

CVEN9881.description: In today's environmentally conscious world, effective hazardous waste management is paramount. Our course offers an in-depth exploration of this vital field, equipping students with the expertise to address this global challenge. This journey begins with waste audits and characterising hazardous waste across diverse regions and industries. You'll grasp the essentials of controlling waste generation, transportation, and manifest systems while also acquiring knowledge about waste minimisation and on-site treatment techniques. We'll further investigate integrated off-site treatment facilities and the responsible management of treatment residues, providing a holistic understanding of waste management. Additionally, we'll introduce you to the intricate planning of regional hazardous waste management systems. You will gain profound insights into the characteristics of various waste types and their impact on industries like steel, pulp and paper, petrochemicals, and food processing. By the course's conclusion, you'll be well-prepared to address the challenges of hazardous waste management and to affect meaningful change across industries and regions globally.
CVEN9881.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9881.title: Hazardous Waste Management

CVEN9885.description:
This course will help students understand the fate of contaminants in the environment. It will help them predict contaminant fate, determine if mitigation measures are required and help them design mitigation measures.

Topics will include: Processes controlling transformation and fate of chemicals in the environment. Measurement and prediction of contaminant behaviour in natural and engineered systems. Fundamentals of dispersion common to all environmental media (air, water, soil). Air chemistry; interaction and degradation of gaseous pollutants in the atmosphere. Dispersion processes; nature of dispersion processes, advection and diffusion. Modelling of dispersion in the atmosphere water bodies and soils.
CVEN9885.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9885.title: Transport and Transformation of Contaminants

CVEN9886.description:
Microbes have been living on this planet for billions of years longer than we have, and they have evolved in all sorts of interesting and useful ways! As engineers, we need to understand how microbes affect natural and constructed systems, how we can use these organisms to improve our engineered processes and how we can mitigate the risks associated with harmful microbes.

CVEN9886 will equip you with the basic knowledge and the tools – critical analysis, teamwork and communication skills – to work on real-world assignments and to be able to collaborate with experts and microbiologists in multidisciplinary projects. You will be equipped to tackle crucial global challenges, including:

- How can we improve water quality and sanitation around the world?

- Can we slow down climate change using microbes?

- How can we leverage microbial processes to protect vulnerable communities and ecosystems?
enrolment_rules_raw: Exclusion: CVEN9884
CVEN9886.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9886.title: Environmental Microbial Processes

CVEN9887.description: This course provides a theoretical background to chemistry in an environmental aquatic context including equilibrium, kinetics, acid-base reactions, alkalinity, carbonate chemistry, gas exchange, redox chemistry, complexes, solid precipitation and dissolution, surface chemistry and organic carbon chemistry. Students will have the opportunity to put lecture material into practise through computer labs.
enrolment_rules_raw: Exclusion: CVEN9884
CVEN9887.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9887.title: Environmental Chemical Processes

CVEN9888.description: An introduction to the spectrum of modern environmentalism and ecologically sustainable development (ESD). This course provides an overview of frameworks and tools currently used to manage environmental responsibilities of products, projects, companies and regions as might be encountered by Engineers. Processes for environmental management systems (EMS) of companies and environmental impact assessment (EIA) of projects are explained and discussed with the use of current case studies. While opportunities for ESD at varying scales (Product, Company, Region, Country) are explored using tools such as Life Cycle Assessment and other materials accounting techniques. You will have the opportunity to apply tools, critique data sources and conclusions and discuss contemporary examples.
enrolment_rules_raw: Exclusion: CVEN4705
CVEN9888.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9888.title: Environmental Management

CVEN9892.description: The design of water and energy systems has advanced from a cost-benefit basis to the incorporation of quantitative assessments of environmental burdens and the human and environmental risks associated with competing options. This course will equip students with the ability to apply life cycle assessment for quantifying environmental burdens, and an understanding of the factors that define human health and environmental risks. The latter include the presence of chemicals and pathogenic organisms, and the reliability of engineered systems.
CVEN9892.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9892.title: Sustainability Assessment and Risk Analysis

CVEN9898.description:
The course provides a theoretical background to the sustainability aspects of water and waste management, transport services, energy supply and distribution. The theory will then be applied to the analysis and design of sustainable infrastructure case studies, involving economic, resource and population constraints.

It provides a regional planning context to the planning and design of infrastructure and provides a series of case studies to illustrate the principles of sustainable infrastructure design.
CVEN9898.school: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
CVEN9898.title: Fundamentals of Sustainable Infrastructure

DATA5002.description: This course introduces students to data visualisation in the areas of statistical analysis and data science. Students will learn how to make their own effective and impactful visualisations using software tools including R. There will be a strong focus on developing the skill of data storytelling: combining data, its visualisation, and a narrative to create a powerful story to drive change. Key topics include visualisation for exploratory and statistical data analysis and interactive visualisations such as dashboards.
enrolment_rules_raw: Enrolment in program 5659 or 5959 or 7659 or 7959 or 8161 or 8719 or 8750 or 8959

exclusions.title: Visualisation and Communication of Health Data

DATA5002.title: Data Visualisation

DATA5011.description:
This course exposes students to research methods in applying data science and decisions techniques to a research project. The project courses serve as a capstone in the Master of Data Science and Decisions program. Students will be required to apply and demonstrate their learning from the courses in the program. It also requires students to present their work in visual and verbal forms including a presentation.

The Data Science and Decisions Project course is done over two terms under the course code DATA5011 and DATA5012. The assessment is a final report which is worth 80% and a presentation worth 20%. The project report is due at the end of DATA5012 and presentation is held at the end of DATA5012. Therefore there is no formal assessment while the student is enrolled in DATA5011.

Please note: Students in the 8959 program have an alternative 12 UOC Masters project course: DATA5925 - Data Science and Decisions Project.  Please visit Handbook for more advice.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in 8959
Prerequisite: Must have successfully completed at least 36 UoC in their current Program
DATA5011.title: Data Science and Decisions Project A

DATA5012.description:
This course exposes students to research methods in applying data science and decisions techniques to a research project. The project courses serve as capstone courses in the Master of Data Science and Decisions program. Students will be required to apply and demonstrate their learning from the courses in the program. It also requires students to present their work in visual and verbal forms including a presentation.

The Data science and decisions project course is done over two terms under the course code DATA5011 and DATA5012. The assessment is a final report which is worth 80% and a presentation worth 20%. The project report is due at the end of DATA5012 and presentation is held at the end of DATA5012. Therefore there is no formal assessment while the student is enrolled in DATA5011.
enrolment_rules_raw: Must be enrolled in 8959
Prerequisite: DATA5011
DATA5012.title: Data Science and Decisions Project B

DATA5925.description:
This course is an opportunity to bring together the skills the students have developed during their Master of Data Science and Decisions program and apply them to a substantive new problem. Students will work in a small group and present results in thesis form and in a presentation. Students will be supervised by an academic staff member from the School and meet one hour per week to discuss and work on the group project.
Note: Available only to students for in the 8959 Master of Data Science and Decisions program.

Students usually complete their project during their last one or two Terms. Students are not eligible to start a project until they have completed at least 36 UoC (typically, 6 courses) over at least three terms.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Must have successfully completed at least 36 UoC in their current Program.
Enrolled in Program 8959 Master of Data Science and Decisions only
DATA5925.title: Data Science and Decisions Project

DATA9001.description:
This course provides a broad overview of Data Science as a platform for further studies in Data Science and an understanding and appreciation of Data Science in the modern world.

Students will study the fundamentals of Data Science as it is applied in Computer Science, Economics, and Mathematics and Statistics. They will be introduced to topics such as databases, data analytics, data mining, Bayesian statistics, statistical software, econometrics, machine learning and business forecasting.

The content of this course will be delivered via weekly live lectures with academics from three different Schools: The School of Mathematics and Statistics, the School of Economics and the School of Computer Science and Engineering. These concepts will be further explored through a series of tutorials/workshops.
enrolment_rules_raw: Enrolment in program 5518 or 5959 or 7959 or 8518 or 8959.
DATA9001.title: Fundamentals of Data Science

DIET4001.description: This is the first of three clinical dietetics subjects where you apply the knowledge you have learned about nutrition through the lifecycle and from human physiology and biochemistry to clinical care. In this course, you will study the special nutritional needs of individuals in community and clinical settings and develop essential skills for safe and effective practice in medical nutrition therapy. These include the ability to provide health education relevant to specific diseases, and manipulate recipes, dietary patterns and overall nutrient and energy intake for individual clients according to their needs
DIET4001.title: Clinical Dietetics and Counselling 1

DIET4002.description: This is the second of three clinical dietetics subjects where you apply the knowledge you have learned about nutrition through the lifecycle and from human physiology and biochemistry to clinical care. In this course, you will build on knowledge and skills from DIET4001 Clinical Dietetics and Counselling 1. You will focus on the medical nutrition therapy for complex and common conditions. You will continue to refine your skills in applying the Nutrition Care Process to safely manage a range of cases with a person-centred approach.  These include the ability to assess clinical priorities, provide health education relevant to specific diseases, counsel behaviour changes and modify recipes, dietary patterns and overall nutrient and energy intake for individual clients according to their needs
enrolment_rules_raw: Pre-requisite: DIET4001
DIET4002.title: Clinical Dietetics and Counselling 2

DIET4003.description: This is the last of three clinical dietetics subjects where you apply the knowledge you have learned about nutrition through the lifecycle and from human physiology and biochemistry to clinical care. In this course, you will continue to build knowledge and skills for inpatient and outpatient dietetic practice, with emphasis on the complexity of care needs in patients with multiple morbidities, and the special needs of paediatric patients. You will learn essential skills that will help enable you to prioritise dietetic care to ensure high quality and safe patient outcomes.
enrolment_rules_raw: Pre-requisite: DIET4001 and DIET4002
DIET4003.title: Clinical Dietetics and Counselling 3

ECON5101.description:
Decision-making by consumers, producers, and governments lies at the heart of economic analysis. It determines how scarce resources are allocated, how markets function, and how welfare is distributed across society.

The first half of this microeconomics course is devoted to the study of decision-making and the modelling of associated market behaviour. We then study how individual economic decisions interact in markets with varying degrees of competition, paying substantial attention to the comparative welfare outcomes produced by different market forms.

Additional topics include externalities, game theory and its applications, and asymmetric information. There is an emphasis on the use of analytical tools and mathematical models, which underpin much of current research in microeconomics.

By the end of the course, students will be able to apply core microeconomic models to analyse decision-making and market outcomes, critically evaluate efficiency and welfare implications across market structures, and use formal tools to address issues such as externalities, strategic interaction, and information asymmetries.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5103 and (COMM5005 or COMM5000 or COMM5501 or DATA9001)
ECON5101.title: Microeconomics

ECON5102.description:
The macroeconomy of a country is a complex network consisting of millions of interacting agents, including consumers, ﬁrms, banks and government institutions. This course introduces you to some of the models employed by economists to understand how these agents interact and contribute to economic growth, the business cycle and other macroeconomic variables.

The course covers a range of topics, including ﬁscal and monetary policies, the business cycle, inflation and unemployment and economic growth models. Models developed in the unit are applied to real-world data and are used to analyse observed developments across different economies.

By the end of the course, you will develop the tools, skills and knowledge necessary for you to operate as a practicing macroeconomist.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5103 and (COMM5005 or COMM5000 or COMM5501). Students in 8412 are excluded from course.
ECON5102.title: Macroeconomics

ECON5103.description:
How do markets operate, how do firms and consumers respond to incentives, and how do government policies affect business strategy and performance?

This course introduces key economic principles and their application to business decision making in a dynamic and uncertain environment. Students will develop a foundational understanding of economic principles and receive practical training in decision making, within the economic contexts which influence business activities.

By the end of the course, students will be able to apply economic reasoning to strategic and operational decisions, assess policy impacts on business outcomes, and think critically about the broader economic forces shaping modern organisations.
ECON5103.title: Business Economics

ECON5106.description:
The valuation of financial assets is a cornerstone of real-world financial markets. The economic theory of financial markets provides a logical foundation for modern asset pricing and portfolio choice theories.

This course provides economic insights into finance and financial markets. We study equilibrium valuation and pricing through the lenses of economic concepts. Major financial instruments such as bonds, stocks, futures, and options are introduced under economic equilibrium context, and we discuss techniques to value these diverse financial assets. We then turn to the "utility-based" approach, wherein a well-defined utility structure is established as a model primitive. Maximising expected utility, we derive optimal consumption, equilibrium trades and prices. In turn, we discuss how trade is beneficial for all the participants in the market. We conclude the course with an introduction to modern portfolio theory.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ((COMM5005 or COMM5000 or COMM5501) and ECON5103) or (enrolment in program 8750 or 8161 or 8719)
ECON5106.title: Economics of Finance

ECON5111.description: Strategic interaction is central to modern economics and business decisions. This course introduces the core tools of game theory and applies them to competition, contracting, auctions, bargaining, and related strategic settings. You will study simultaneous and sequential games, imperfect information, and repeated interaction, and apply these tools across mean cases and contexts. The result is a practical framework for analysing strategic behaviour. By the end of this course, you will be able apply core game theoretic concepts to analyse strategic behaviour, market structure, and policy design with precision and confidence.​
enrolment_rules_raw: Pre-requisite: ECON5103
ECON5111.title: Economics of Strategy

ECON5205.description:
What can we learn from data, and how can we separate correlation and causality?

This course introduces the use of econometrics to explore and estimate economic relationships using linear regression models. Emphasis will be placed on cross-sectional data and on understanding the conditions required for inferring causal relationships. We will also consider extensions that address common data analysis complications, including heteroskedasticity, proxy variables, and other data limitations. And we will consider regression models for time series and panel data, highlighting their relevance for economic analysis. Practical computer-based exercises are integrated throughout, enabling students to gain hands-on experience working with real-world data and econometric software.

By the end of the course, you will have the skills to critically interpret empirical relationships and a foundation for more advanced courses in econometrics.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite or corequisite: (ECON5103 and (COMM5005 or COMM5000 or COMM5501)) OR enrolment in program 8959.
ECON5205.title: Econometrics

ECON5206.description: This course provides the framework for modelling financial time series data, such as commodity/asset prices, interest rates or exchange rates. You will learn the key characteristics of financial data, concepts of volatility and risk, modelling time varying volatility, risk management, and relationships among financial series. The knowledge and methods acquired in this course are particularly useful and sought after in the public and private macroeconomic and financial sectors.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (ECON5205 or ECON5248 or MATH5905) or (enrol in program 8161 or 8719)
ECON5206.title: Financial Econometrics

ECON5209.description:
How can we bridge the gap between academic learning and real-world economic practice, and apply theory and quantitative tools to policy and business challenges?

In this course, students apply their accumulated understanding of economic theories and quantitative methods to analyse complex, real-world challenges defined by industry and government partners. In doing so, they turn real-world data into evidence-based policy advice.

This practicum is structured around collaboration with industry and government partners, offering authentic challenges that deepen analytical and problem-solving skills. Communication skills are built through this collaborative work and direct stakeholder engagement.

By the end of the course, students will be able to independently design and execute applied economic research, evaluate complex policy issues using data-driven methods, and communicate analytical insights effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
enrolment_rules_raw: Corequisite: ECON5210
Prerequisite: ECON5101 and ECON5102 and ECON5205 and 42 UOC overall
ECON5209.title: Economics Practicum

ECON5210.description:
How can we bridge the gap between academic learning and real-world economic practice, and apply theory and quantitative tools to policy and business challenges?

This course provides you with the opportunity to reflect on the Economics Practicum through the economist’s lens. The course should be taken concurrently with the Economics Practicum course (ECON5209). It complements the hands-on economics practicum by focusing on critical reflection, professional development, and the communication of economic findings. Students will consolidate their learning and articulate the value of the practicum experience.

By the end of the course, students will feel well prepared for roles that require rigorous analysis of economic policies, data-driven decision-making, and communicating insights to policy stakeholders.
enrolment_rules_raw: Corequisite: ECON5209.
Prerequisite: ECON5101, ECON5102, ECON5205 and 18 UOC of Economics Electives.

equivalents.title: Waiver for ECON5210 Reflections on Practicum Through the Economist's Lens

ECON5210.title: Reflections on Practicum through the Economist’s Lens

ECON5248.description:
Building, evaluating, and interpreting forecasting models for both short-term and long-term applications is the key to understanding and predicting the dynamics of an economy.

This course looks at the use of econometric and statistical techniques relevant to forecasting in a business environment and computer implementation of the methods: Both short-term forecasting with simple time series models, and longer-term forecasting that include seasonal and trend terms are considered. Applied work using a statistical software package is emphasised in this non-specialist course. 

By the end of the course, students will be able to design, implement, and critically assess forecasting models that support strategic decision-making in dynamic market environments. Through hands-on exercises and data-driven analysis, they will gain the ability to translate quantitative results into meaningful business insights.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (COMM5005 or DATA9001) OR (enrolment in program 8750 or 8161 or 8719)
ECON5248.title: Business Forecasting

ECON5258.description:
Successful business leadership depends on understanding both the economic forces that shape markets and the data that inform strategic choices.

This course equips students with the ability to interpret economic trends, apply decision-making frameworks, and use data-driven insights to guide policy and business strategy. It covers the policy and strategic aspects of business management and also provides a practical and analytical approach to economic policy issues. It is structured into two parts. The first part (Economics) provides you with the tools to use economic principles in decision-making and an understanding of the broader economic environment in which business decisions must be made. The second part (Data Analysis) introduces the basic statistical tools and quantitative methods useful in understanding the types of data encountered in business.

By the end of the course, students will be able to analyse economic and business data, evaluate policy implications, and make informed, evidence-based decisions in complex business environments.
ECON5258.title: Introductory Economics and Data Analysis for Business Professionals

ECON5301.description: This course delves into the theoretical underpinnings of financial crises, offering an advanced exploration of the factors that contribute to financial instability. Building on prior courses in microeconomics, macroeconomics, and game theory, this course will examine the role of market frictions, with a particular focus on asymmetric information, liquidity constraints, and incomplete markets. You will gain a comprehensive understanding of the mechanisms leading to financial crises and the tools necessary to analyze and mitigate these events.
enrolment_rules_raw: Pre-requisite: ECON5101
ECON5301.title: Markets and Frictions

ECON5304.description:
​​In today’s global economy, national policies and outcomes are deeply interconnected. 

​This course introduces the core concepts and analytical tools of open-economy macroeconomics, providing a structured framework for examining how countries interact through trade, capital flows, and policy choices. It covers exchange rate determination, balance of payments, current account imbalances, international asset markets, and the role of fiscal and monetary policy in open economies. It also considers the functioning of different exchange rate regimes, the challenges of monetary unions, and the causes and consequences of international financial crises. Emphasis is placed on applying theory to contemporary issues and policy debates, enabling students to better interpret real-world events and understand the constraints and trade-offs faced by policymakers. 

​By the end of this course, you will be able to analyse macroeconomic dynamics with formal models and evaluate fiscal and monetary policy in domestic and international settings.​
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5102
ECON5304.title: International Macroeconomics

ECON5306.description:
When so many economic decisions are taken by political actors, understanding the economy also means understanding the interactions between politics and economics.

This course covers theory, evidence and current issues at the intersection between economics and political science.

Topics considered include economic theories of the state, regime changes and revolutions, voting theory, interest group politics, corruption, the democratic peace, and electoral competition.

By the end of the course, you will have the skills relevant in understanding the delicate interplay between economics and politics.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5101
ECON5306.title: Politics and Economics

ECON5310.description:
​​Why do some countries grow and prosper while others remain trapped in poverty? Poverty and underdevelopment remain central global economic challenges. This course provides an in-depth exploration of competing explanations of underdevelopment and current strategies for promoting development. You will examine the roles of institutions, institutional change, markets, and policy in shaping development outcomes, with close attention to both domestic and international contexts. A key focus is the interaction between theory and evidence, including how to assess whether specific interventions are likely to improve welfare.

By the end of this course, you will be able to analyse major drivers of underdevelopment, design innovative ways to assess development policies with theory and evidence, and identify credible pathways for improving outcomes.​
enrolment_rules_raw: Pre-requisite: ECON5103 OR MNGT5201 or approval of the PG Coordinator
ECON5310.title: Development Economics

ECON5316.description:
What determines who gains and who loses in global trade and how governments should respond? International trade shapes economic growth, wages, inequality, and the success or failure of businesses. This course develops an advanced, analytically rigorous analysis of trade theory and trade policy, supported by empirical evidence. You analyse models of comparative advantage, technology differences, factor endowments, and economies of scale to understand how these forces influence trade patterns and income distribution. You will also evaluate the effects of key policy tools and develop practical problem-solving skills for trade analysis.

By the end of this course, you will be able to use trade models and empirical evidence to assess policy choices, explain their implications, communicate clear, defensible policy recommendations.​
enrolment_rules_raw: Pre-requisite: ECON5101
ECON5316.title: International Trade Theory and Policy

ECON5321.description:
What drives the behaviour of firms and industry dynamics in the modern economic landscape?

This course studies the behaviour of firms and industry sectors, with a focus on competition outcomes and market dynamics. Through an exploration of market structures (including perfect competition, monopoly, and oligopoly), dynamic strategic interaction, price discrimination, product differentiation, advertising, entry and predation, it connects theoretical concepts with real-world relevance.

By the end of the course, you will develop a deep understanding of the economic forces at play in real-world markets and how they come together to drive economic policy.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5101 or ECON5111
ECON5321.title: Industrial Organisation

ECON5323.description: This course studies the internal organisation of firms and other organisations. It provides a rigorous introduction to foundational theories, and then discusses applications to real-world managerial problems. How should incentives be designed in organisations? How should conflict within an organisation be resolved? When should organisations outsource and when should they produce internally? Why do organisations arise in market economies? Tools from game theory, information economics and contract theory are introduced and applied to analyse these (and other) questions.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5101 OR ECON5103
ECON5323.title: Organisational Economics

ECON5324.description:
​​Standard economic theory assumes that people have correct beliefs based on correct statistical reasoning, that they are narrowly self-interested, and that they manage to maximise their utility. Decades of experimental evidence suggest a more complicated picture. People systematically misperceive probabilities, cooperate with strangers in ways that sacrifice their own material payoffs, and make choices that they themselves deem suboptimal. Explaining these empirical regularities requires new theory.

​In this course, students will study the core findings of behavioural economics, learn the formal theoretical frameworks developed to explain it, and build the empirical reasoning skills needed to critically evaluate competing accounts. Topics include reference-dependent preferences and prospect theory, intertemporal choice, risk preferences, bounded rationality, social preferences, behavioural game theory, and behavioural public policy.

​By the end of this course, you will be able to formulate behavioural hypotheses precisely, evaluate them using appropriate theoretical tools, and critically assess the evidence used to support or challenge them.​
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5103
ECON5324.title: Behavioural Economics

ECON5327.description: The environment is one of the most important and most debated modern policy issues. This course provides an economic perspective on this debate. We will discuss the reasons behind why environmental problems exist, why unregulated markets sometimes fail in this context, and potential economic solutions to these problems, which include regulations, taxes, subsidies, and pollution permit trading schemes. We will also cover methods for determining the benefits and costs of environmental preservation. The course will equip you with the necessary knowledge to take part in the discussion about environmental policy from an economic perspective.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5101
ECON5327.title: Environmental Economics

ECON5403.description: The course offers a broad interdisciplinary perspective on econometrics, data science, statistical and machine learning methods through the lens of econometric theory and applications. The course emphasises the links between the theory, computational methods, and the application of the models to real examples. Being equipped with this knowledge will enable you to conduct a broad range of econometric modelling tasks.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5205
ECON5403.title: Econometric Theory and Machine Learning

ECON5408.description:
Applied econometrics provides the tools to transform raw data into meaningful economic insight. It bridges theory and evidence, allowing us to rigorously test hypotheses, identify causal relationships, and inform real-world policy and business decisions.

This course builds from preliminary investigations of linear regression models to introduce more advanced econometric techniques. Topics include limited-dependent variable models, treatment of endogeneity, time series econometrics and panel data. Special emphasis will be placed on the process and potential pitfalls of conducting and evaluating applied econometric research.

By the end of the course, you will be equipped with the necessary knowledge to be able to conduct your own econometric research using standard real-world economic and business data.
enrolment_rules_raw: Pre-requisite: ECON5205
ECON5408.title: Applied Econometric Methods

ECON6202.description:
How can we measure the impact of economic interventions? Why do some policies succeed while others fail? 

This course provides the powerful tools of causal inference that can answer such questions. It covers foundational methods for identifying causal effects—including randomised controlled trials, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, and regression discontinuity designs—to equip students with the skills to critically evaluate empirical research and conduct their own rigorous analyses. 

By the end of the course, you will be able to evaluate and apply causal inference methods to real data to measure the effects of a wide range of policies and programs. Whether you are interested in public policy, labour markets, health, development, or finance, mastering causal inference will enhance their ability to make informed data-driven decisions and produce credible economic analysis.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5408, or enrolment in 8959 Data Science and Decisions and completion of ECON5103, or Corequisite: COMM8102
ECON6202.title: Empirical Methods for Causal Inference

ECON6309.description:
This course covers the theory and practice of economic measurement, including the measurement of key economic indicators such as the Consumer Price Index, Gross Domestic Product and productivity growth. 

Approaches employed by international statistical agencies will be highlighted, along with the possibility that policy implications are often reliant on the choice of measurement techniques. The course will be technically rigorous, particularly in the use of microeconomic theory and econometric analysis, and will draw on the latest international research developments.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5101
ECON6309.title: Economic Measurement

ECON6312.description: This course exposes you to the possibilities for welfare gains available through the thoughtful application of insights from behavioural economics to adjust incentives in a variety of real-world settings. The study of applications will be preceded and motivated through a consideration of the gaps in mainstream economic theory and the developing ways that behavioural economics attempts to fill these gaps. Through a combination of exploring frontier behavioural economics theory and working through case studies of the application of behavioural economics to a series of real-world policy interventions in Australia and abroad, you will gain an understanding of the power of theoretically-grounded behavioural economics insights to enhance traditional economic understanding and improve the stewardship of modern economies.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5103 OR MNGT5201 or approval of the PG Coordinator
ECON6312.title: Policy Applications of Behavioural Economics

ECON6313.description:
This course investigates the role of the public sector in the economic arena. It explains where in the economy government intervention is needed and why; how this intervention influences the behaviour of actors in the private sector; and the welfare effects of such intervention. The course also applies a political economy lens to understand how and why behaviour in the public sector is determined not only by economic concerns but also by political processes. Specific topics to be covered include welfare economics, optimal taxation, market failure, economic regulation, industrial policy, and political economy. 

You will also have the opportunity to learn more exotic topics such as collusion, financial stability, and shadow banks, through several video lectures. These mini lectures provide a more complete picture of government policy and cover real-world topics that are not often discussed in a public economics course.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON5101 OR ECON5111 OR MNGT5201 OR approval of the PG Coordinator
ECON6313.title: Public Economics and Regulation

ECON7001.description:
Understanding how individuals and firms make optimal decisions and how their interactions shape market outcomes is paramount. It underpins much of modern economics, helping explain and predict behaviour under different market structures and information conditions.

This course deals with individual optimal decision making and equilibrium. Fundamental topics covered include rational choice, utility maximisation, expenditure minimisation, production theory, and decision making under uncertainty. Partial equilibrium, game theory and non-competitive environments will also be covered. The course also explores economic environments with asymmetric information, including auctions and screening.

By the end of the course, you will be able to formally analyse strategic and non-strategic interactions in economic settings using microeconomic theory.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (ECON7004 AND Enrolment in program 1540, 1561 or 8635) or Approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7001.title: Microeconomic Theory I

ECON7002.description:
​​This is an advanced course in macroeconomic theory. The first part of the course will briefly review business cycle facts, real business cycle models, and useful tools and technique. The second part of the course will cover the New Keynesian approach to macroeconomics, covering topics such as monetary policy and inflation, the real effects of monetary policy, the advantages of credible policy commitments and monetary-fiscal interactions.

By the end of this course, you will be able to analyse macroeconomic dynamics with formal models and evaluate fiscal and monetary policy in a wide range of environments.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (ECON7004 and Enrolment in program 1540, 1561 or 8635) or Approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7002.title: Macroeconomic Theory I

ECON7004.description:
Mathematical economics is essential because it provides the formal tools to express economic ideas, uncover relations not easily observed through intuition alone, and engage confidently with modern economic research and policy analysis.

This course offers a rigorous introduction to mathematical economics. It equips students with the tools to analyse optimisation and equilibrium in diverse economic settings. Building on core concepts such as sets, functions, normed spaces, linear algebra, and calculus, students will apply mathematical techniques including advanced optimisation, fixed point theory, and comparative statics to analyse a range of economic problems. Emphasis is placed on both mathematical formalism and the intuition needed to apply these results in economics.

By the end of the course, students will be equipped to engage deeply with analytical economic models and have a rigorous foundation for advanced economic analysis.
enrolment_rules_raw:
Enrolment in program 1540 or 1561 or 8635 or
Approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7004.title: Mathematical Economics

ECON7101.description: This course introduces basic tools and topics in microeconomic theory, in particular, market design. The course is intended both for graduate students who wish to develop a solid background in microeconomics to pursue research in applied fields and for students who seek to specialise in economic theory. The course covers a broad array of topics analysed through the lens of auction theory and mechanism design. Most of our time in this course will be spent on economic applications, but there will be some sections where we need also to develop some new tools.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON7001 or Approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7101.title: Microeconomic Theory II

ECON7102.description: This course is an introduction into solving and analyzing macroeconomic models. The course begins with linearization techniques and perturbation. We then move on to covering non-linear approximations of model solutions. In addition to solving macroeconomic models, students will also learn how to parameterize them. Towards this end, we discuss not only calibration, but also the basics of estimation such as the Kalman filter and Maximum Likelihood estimation. Finally, the course also provides a glimpse at models with heterogeneous agents. Throughout the course we will discuss how our macroeconomic models can be used for economic (policy) analysis.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: (ECON7002 and Enrolment in program 1540, 1561 or 8635) or approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7102.title: Macroeconomic Theory II

ECON7202.description:
How can we measure the impact of economic interventions? Why do some policies succeed while others fail? 

This course provides the powerful tools of causal inference that can answer such questions. It covers foundational methods for identifying causal effects—including randomised controlled trials, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, and regression discontinuity designs—to equip students with the skills to critically evaluate empirical research and conduct their own rigorous analyses.  

By the end of the course, you will be able to evaluate and apply causal inference methods to real data to measure the effects of a wide range of policies and programs. Whether you are interested in public policy, labour markets, health, development, or finance, mastering causal inference will enhance their ability to make informed data-driven decisions and produce credible economic analysis.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: COMM8102 or approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7202.title: Empirical Methods for Causal Inference

ECON7204.description:
​​This course will provide you with an introduction to econometrics as it is applied in macroeconomics. Emphasis is on hands-on implementation of the methods covered in the course. Topics include macroeconomic data, linear and nonlinear time series models, practical issues with likelihood-based inference for these models, forecast evaluation, structural identification and use of micro data in empirical macroeconomics.

By the end of this course, you will be able to implement core macroeconometric methods, evaluate model assumptions, and draw defensible conclusions from aggregate data in order to undertake modern macroeconomic research.​
enrolment_rules_raw: Corequisite or Prerequisite: COMM8102 or approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7204.title: Macroeconometrics

ECON7205.description:
​​This course covers advanced econometric methods for empirical research in applied microeconomics and related fields. You will study recent developments in widely used causal research designs, along with complementary approaches for policy and program evaluation. Applications are drawn from labour, development, political economy, education, and health. The course prepares you both to conduct research using state-of-the-art microeconometric methods and to critically evaluate empirical studies.

​By the end of this course, you will be able to apply modern empirical methods, assess identification and model choices critically, and communicate evidence with precision.
ECON7205.title: Microeconometrics

ECON7301.description: The main goal of this course is to provide you with a set of tools and knowledge that would enable you to critically read recent research papers and conduct your own original research in industrial organisation. In particular, we investigate how firms exercise market power in a variety of settings and how the government may curb the negative side effects of this through regulation. We will develop rigorous theoretical models maintaining their close connections to reality, elaborate on the economic logic and intuition behind the analyses, and discuss real-world implications. The course emphasises the importance of a theoretical understanding of strategic behaviour as the foundation for any practical application to industry.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON7001 and ECON7004 or approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7301.title: Industrial Organisation

ECON7309.description: This course covers the theory and practice of economic measurement, including the measurement of key economic indicators such as the Consumer Price Index, Gross Domestic Product and productivity growth. Approaches employed by international statistical agencies will be highlighted, along with the possibility that policy implications are often reliant on the choice of measurement techniques. The course will be technically rigorous, particularly in the use of microeconomic theory and econometric analysis, and will draw on the latest international research developments.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: ECON7001 and ECON7004 or approval from PG coordinators of Economics
ECON7309.title: Economic Measurement

EDST5024.description:
Strong communication skills are essential for success in learning and crucial for effective teaching. In this course you will be equipped with effective communication skills for interacting with a range of stakeholders in education contexts, including peers, colleagues, students and university staff. You will also learn how to effectively employ different text types and modes of communication.

The course has a particular focus on developing capabilities in reading and writing texts common in education contexts. The course also focuses on increasing your confidence and effectiveness in a range of oral communication activities, including class discussions, online interactions, collaborative group activities and class presentations.

This elective course is open to all students enrolled in postgraduate Education programs. It is recommended that students complete this course as early as possible in their program as it will support their engagement and success in other postgraduate Education courses.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program.
EDST5024.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5024.title: Effective Communication in Education Contexts

EDST5099.description: In this course you are introduced to UNSW study skills, procedures, academic expectations and educational research. The course aims to increase your knowledge and understanding of communication, research and study skills to assist you in developing an understanding of university expectations as a postgraduate student. You will develop essential study skills through learning about and writing about UNSW academic expectations and educational research.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in the 96 UOC or 72 UOC plan of a Master of Education or Master of Educational Leadership
EDST5099.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5099.title: Foundation 1: University Study Skills in Education

EDST5100.description: In this course you are introduced to topics in Education. This course aims to introduce you to the main specialisations of Education and to assist you in better understanding Education. The course has a particular focus on the specialised streams in the Master of Education. You will develop an understanding in the various specialisations that define Education. These include Curriculum and Assessment, Educations Studies, Education Systems, Gifted Education, TESOL, Special Education and Educational Psychology.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in the 96 UOC or 72 UOC plan of a Master of Education or Master of Educational Leadership
EDST5100.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5100.title: Foundation 2: Fields of Practice in Education

EDST5101.description: In this course you will learn about quantitative research methods and data analysis at an advanced level. The course will cover research design, population/sampling selection, construction of data collection tools, various types of data collection methods, and data analysis such as multiple regression and factor analysis. Emphasis will be given to the selection of statistical analyses that would be appropriate for different types of quantitative data.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Applied Linguistics program. Or EDST5448 or EDST5458 and enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program
EDST5101.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5101.title: Advanced Quantitative Research

EDST5106.description:
The focus of this course is on applied behaviour analysis, and how it is accomplished through the use of functional behavioural assessment and skills training.

You will learn about the models, theories, and philosophies that form the basis of sound inclusive educational and behavioural practice. You will learn how to assess behaviour, teach new skills, and manage behaviour, both academic and social. The strengths and weaknesses of common school practices for decreasing students' inappropriate behaviour will be discussed, and strategies for promoting prosocial behaviour will be described. You will practice collecting and analysing data and use this information to write behavioural intervention plans. You will also use the knowledge gained in the course to design and implement a social skills training lesson.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: EDST5133 and enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760.
EDST5106.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5106.title: Advanced Behaviour Support Strategies

EDST5107.description: The focus of this course is on students with high-incidence disabilities. In this course, students will be presented with cognitive, perceptual, language, academic learning, and social-emotional characteristics of these populations. Issues in assessment, curriculum and instruction, and placement will also be discussed. This course will provide students with instruction on applying the goals, intervention strategies, and procedures related to psychodynamic, behavioural, biophysical, and ecological approaches to individuals with disabilities.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.
EDST5107.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5107.title: Teaching Methods for High Incidence Disabilities

EDST5111.description: Students with intellectual disabilities face numerous challenges in educational environments. You will learn about characteristics of students with intellectual disabilities (including issues of definition), relevant legislative requirements, and how to use assessment for educational intervention. You will learn about effective evidence-based practices that you can use to assist students with intellectual disabilities accomplish their educational goals. You will learn about curriculum-based strategies and curriculum adjustments and modifications that you can use in your teaching practice. In this course, great emphasis is placed on a life-span approach to people with intellectual disabilities and their families; and why it is important for professionals to have a holistic perspective. Thus, you will also learn about issues related to social and community inclusion, family, peer and partner relationships of people with intellectual disabilities. You will become acquainted with issues and supports relevant to adults with intellectual disabilities. Throughout the course, you will also learn about the importance of diverse transitions in the lives of people with intellectual disabilities and how these can be supported.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760
EDST5111.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5111.title: Intellectual Disabilities

EDST5112.description: One of the central needs of a teacher is to understand how their students learn. In this course, you will learn about how people learn generally, the degree to which people differ in how they learn, and the strategies required to teach them effectively. You will study core educational psychology topics - including development, cognition, and motivation - and observe them in action in classrooms. In assessment, you will articulate these issues, and report on observations of teaching in a way that bridges theory, research, and practice.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs; 8926 Master of Teaching (Secondary), 8913 Master of Education, or 8963 Master of Educational Leadership
EDST5112.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5112.title: Learning: Psychological and Social Perspectives

EDST5113.description: Students on the autism spectrum face immense challenges in educational environments. You will engage with current knowledge about characteristics and effective evidence-based practices used to assist students on the autism spectrum to accomplish their educational goals. You will engage with theories, societal attitudes, legislation, and policy to develop your professional judgments and teaching practices. You will learn instructional and curriculum-based strategies and curriculum adjustments that you can use in your teaching practice. You will also learn about challenges faced by families of students on the autism spectrum, and learn effective strategies to promote home-school collaboration. You will become acquainted with issues and supports relevant to adults on the autism spectrum.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.
EDST5113.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5113.title: Students on the Autism Spectrum

EDST5114.description: In this course, you will examine how the policies and practices of today connect with historical contexts, traditions, ideologies and beliefs about curriculum and assessment and how future developments are shaped by events and decisions made in the past. The course covers key issues, policies and events that have shaped reform agendas in the development of curriculum and assessment in New South Wales and Australia on a national level and will consider how these compare to developments internationally. You will be given the opportunity to research, analyse and discuss issues in curriculum and assessment of interest to you.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.
EDST5114.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5114.title: Curriculum and Assessment

EDST5115.description:
This course explores the historical, political and social context of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education in Australia and critically examines the social and societal factors that shape Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students’ experiences and outcomes. It introduces you to current research, theoretical frameworks and practical strategies to help in developing your skills and knowledge to critically reflect on and respond to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students’ issues in education.  The central focus of the course is to prepare you to meet the Australian Professional Standards that directly concern Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education: the teaching of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students (AITSL 1.4), and the embedding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, histories and heritage across the curriculum (AITSL 2.4). 

This course includes a three-day intensive “on Country” Immersion Program which will introduce and engage you with local Aboriginal communities, cultures and perspectives, to help raise your awareness about the need for a focus on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives in schools and in teacher education. Successful completion of this course requires you to satisfactorily complete the Immersion Program.  More details will be available on Moodle.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs, 8925 or 8926
EDST5115.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5115.title: Indigenous Contexts of Education

EDST5117.description: In this course you will examine the professional issues faced by first year teachers, including the culture of isolation (characteristic of many schools); transition shock; workload issues; and classroom management challenges. Strategies for addressing these challenges will be explored. These include mentoring, peer support, problem-based discussion groups, and the sharing of personal narratives and dialogue through face-to-face and online forums.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: EDST6760
EDST5117.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5117.title: Professional Inquiry

EDST5118.description: In this course, you will complete 25 days of advanced professional practice, including high-level teaching, observation and critical reflection in the area of special education, together with peer observations and school-based fieldwork. You will gain an advanced level of knowledge and skills in teaching students with special needs, and as a graduate of the program, you will meet the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers in the area of professional practice.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: 24 uoc overall, and enrolment in a Special Education specialisation in a postgraduate Education program. Students must have completed EDST5106 or complete EDST5106 concurrently. Consent required.
EDST5118.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5118.title: Professional Practice for Special Education

EDST5120.description: You will explore, and learn to critique, qualitative research in education; and you will be introduced to some key methodological issues by looking at published and unpublished qualitative writing across different sub-fields of educational research. You will learn about different epistemological and methodological approaches, and, by the end of the course, you will have a good awareness of the issues and components you need to design a small-scale qualitative research project of your own.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Applied Linguistics program. Or EDST5448 or EDST5458 and enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program
EDST5120.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5120.title: Advanced Qualitative Research

EDST5127.description: In this course you will focus on the role that learning conversations, mentoring and coaching can play in the development of teachers. Models and perspectives on coaching and mentoring will be explored, as well as the development of listening and reflection skills. Action research by students will provide feedback on the various models of mentoring and coaching.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program
EDST5127.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5127.title: Coaching and Mentoring in Educational Leadership

EDST5129.description: In this course, students will be provided with an overview of the numerous transitions students with disabilities face. The focus of the course will be on the preparation, support and planning required for transitioning students with disabilities. Contemporary legislation, polices, methods and service delivery for the education and transitional programming for students with disabilities at different levels (early childhood to primary level, primary to secondary level, secondary to tertiary level, secondary level to vocation) will be discussed.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed EDST6761 or EDST6765
EDST5129.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5129.title: Transitions in the Lives of Students with Disabilities

EDST5131.description: In this course, you will explore current theories underlying oral communication skills, focusing in particular on the learning and teaching of second or additional language learners in schools, both locally and internationally. Topics include theoretical and practical perspectives on oral communication across the curriculum; cognitive and metacognitive processes involved in speaking and listening; issues of intelligibility and pronunciation; genres of speaking and implications for listening; learning and teaching students for whom English is a second language or dialect planning; developing oral communication tasks and activities; assessing speaking and listening in the content areas.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760
EDST5131.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5131.title: Oral Communication Across the Curriculum

EDST5133.description: In this course you will draw on a variety of theoretical and practical perspectives, principles and research to provide pre-service teachers with a depth and breadth of knowledge that will enable professional decision-making and practice in establishing classroom management and ensuring student engagement in learning.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs, 8925 Master of Teaching (Primary) or 8926 Master of Teaching (Secondary) or 8913 Masters of Education or 8963 Educational Leadership
EDST5133.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5133.title: Creating Engaging Learning Environments

EDST5134.description: In this course you will survey the characteristics, training, and educational needs of students with disabilities, gifts and talents, and culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, emphasising accommodating students with diverse needs in inclusive settings. This includes legal mandates and regulations; characteristics and educational needs of students with diverse needs; and practical, research-based instructional techniques that can be used with these students in the general education classroom.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs, 8925 or 8926
EDST5134.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5134.title: Supporting Diverse Learners: Inclusive Practices

EDST5138.description: This course will provide an overview of the principles, policies, and philosophies underpinning inclusion. The Universal Design for Learning approach to curriculum design for students with disabilities or diverse needs will be a central focus as well as evidence and research-based approaches to teaching these students in mainstream school settings. The role of teachers, special educators, and the leadership team in promoting the successful inclusion of students with diverse needs will also be highlighted.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed EDST6761 or EDST6765
EDST5138.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5138.title: Inclusive Education: Policy, Planning and Pedagogy

EDST5139.description: The course will engage in a substantive exploration of the relationships between language, literacy, and numeracy, assessment and student learning. The course will draw on theory, research and practice related to assessing and teaching students with diverse language and literacy backgrounds and skills in a variety of secondary school contexts.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 8926 Master of Teaching (Secondary)
EDST5139.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5139.title: Language, Literacy and Numeracy

EDST5141.description: In this course, you will be immersed in the competing and politicised discourses and school level practices that play a part in what is known as Indigenous education in Australia. The aim of the course is to equip you with skills, knowledge and the confidence that will support you in becoming an active and aware contributor to improving teaching practices and learning outcomes within the Indigenous education landscape. Informed by ideas and strategies coming from a range of theoretical frameworks, you will critically engage with the literature and research that underpins Indigenous education, challenging you to reflexively position yourself within this landscape as active agents of change.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program
EDST5141.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5141.title: Critically Engaging with Indigenous Education

EDST5142.description: The claim that context matters is ubiquitous in education. What that means and how it plays out in the provision of education across the lifespan and within and beyond traditional education sites is far less known. This course is designed to deepen your understanding of the intimate relations between education and context. Whether you work in early childhood, schools, tertiary environments or non-traditional spaces (e.g., health, military, non-for-profit, corporates), understanding contexts is imperative to achieving the best possible outcomes. This requires you to think beyond the boundaries of any individual educational site and consider the interplay of demography, geolocation, socio-economic status, access to services, among others, and the provision of education. To do this, you will systematically engage with large-scale education and social data to bring to life the theoretical and conceptual tools necessary to analyse, evaluate, problematise and reconstruct the provision of education.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program
EDST5142.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5142.title: Education in Context

EDST5147.description: This course is aimed at postgraduate research students to evaluate and develop their thesis writing abilities and skills. Weekly sessions cover the overall structuring of the thesis; writing the introduction; the literature review; the methodology chapter; discussion chapters; the conclusion; and the abstract. It also covers examiner expectations, with an emphasis on managing the writing process over an extended time period and on managing large amounts of texts. The course is informed by current applied linguistic and educational research into advanced academic and professional writing. It includes writing a conference paper, a journal article, and preparing for seminar/conference presentations.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program
EDST5147.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5147.title: Thesis Writing and Presentation

EDST5150.description:
In this course, you will update and deepen your skills as a language and literacy teacher in the following areas: the nature of language as a phenomenon; language form, meaning and use; language analysis at sentence and supra-sentential levels, oracy and literacy and differences and similarities between spoken and written forms of language; first and second language acquisition and implications for teaching; an overview of the structural grammar of English, focusing on the verb phrase (tense and aspect), modality, and cohesion; scholarship of teacher language awareness.

You will be introduced to these ideas through a variety of texts and activity types and referring to a range of recent and seminal scholarly and practitioner voices within the literature in this area.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.
EDST5150.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5150.title: Teacher Language Awareness

EDST5151.description: How do primary-aged students develop and learn? What, and who, informs their learning? What is the role of cognition, motivation, identity, language, gender, culture, and ability? Using educational psychology as a foundation, you will explore psychological and social perspectives on child development and learning during the primary years of schooling. In order to develop your understanding of young students and how they learn, this course will focus on integrating research findings, theoretical positions, and practical aspects of child development. Specifically, you will be challenged to consider critical developmental issues in relation to your within-school experiences. Completion of this course will enable you to link learning theories and educational practice as a basis for ongoing professional reflection and development of effective primary school pedagogy.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 8925 Master of Teaching (Primary)
EDST5151.faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
EDST5151.title: Child Development: Psychological and Social Perspectives

EDST5155.description: This course enables you to describe fundamental concepts, principles, theories, and terminology used in the main branches of education systems research, policy and practice, and apply that knowledge to new and complex environments. This course explicitly brings international and national commitments, legislation, and policy pillars together to develop robust system design principles and to audit and prosecute reforms. The course is of value to current and aspiring systemic personnel and those wanting to better understand how systems work at scale.
enrolment_rules_raw: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program
